original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Decide whether BIT.md section 4's ordinary interchange runs its recursive or elementary branch at the #4174 reservoir width H = r_max G, by evaluating the wrapper test 2k >= e (or body width below 64) exactly at every q-ary width.
scope_change_reason: PR #4938 open question 1 asks whether one ordinary H-bit interchange fits O(V H^(1-a) + V) at the actual #4174 width. The callee's statement is uniform in width, so the remaining content is which branch the callee takes at that width. This package computes the exact branch threshold and compares it with H. It does not price the elementary algorithm's constant, the three-field placement, or any other CRT step.
bottleneck_link: The CRT layer's saving a - 2(1-epsilon) assumes the interchange's h^(-a) gain. Below the computed width the callee realizes no gain. That holds at the production plan and at every #4174 layout with L below 100 times the threshold. The asymptotic statement is unchanged, and so is the selected frontier.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact threshold, its all-width monotonicity argument and the comparison with H on the two cited #4174 layouts. Do not build an interchange, price constants or revisit placement.
author: James Reed

open_questions.question: Does the CRT layer's claimed saving survive with the interchange's actual threshold, i.e. at which reservoir length does the composed O(V p^(1-a) ell^2 polylog p) bill first improve on the elementary-callee bill, once the K = O(ell + log p) colors and O(ell log d) layers are counted?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Below L = 2,770,641,200 bits every reservoir interchange is elementary, so any CRT-layer saving below that size must come from elsewhere.
open_questions.first_step: Write the per-layer cost with an elementary callee as c_el V H and with a recursive callee as C V H^(1-a2), and find the smallest #4174 layout where the recursive form is smaller for a stated ratio C/c_el.
open_questions.blocked_by: The constants C and c_el are not stated in BIT.md; any answer is conditional on a stated ratio.
